notes.title: WW2 Rebuilder | Patch 1.5.1
notes.content:
This patch fixes some issues on the new Remagen level, and also removes bugs that came out with the DLC launch.

Some of the level-specific changes may appear on the player's side only after a hard restart of that level.

CHANGELOG
[list]
[*] Adjusted collision that was blocking the path in the underground tunnel on RAF Lympne level
[*] Fixed the bug allowing players to destroy the house with the tank on Remagen level before moving the wreck out, which blocked player’s progress
[*] Added missing roof models on Remagen level
[*] Added fixable ceiling in Remagen train station corridor
[*] Blocked of the balconies on Remagen level, that could’ve caused players to stuck
[*] Fixed background NPC spawns on Remagen level
[*] Adjusted wheels placement in one of vehicle props
[*] Various minor fixes
[/list]

[*] Exit from Sandbox mode leads to Poland map now
[*] Fixed crash that sometimes occurred on starting a new mission

[*] Translations bug fixes

Re-designed factory elements that require transport to collect zone.
[*] [b] London [/b]
Increased size of cut decals on airplane that is require to be cut. 
[*] [b] Lympne [/b]
Wing flaps are now available to be craft or build in the workshop table. 
[*] [b] Necropolis [/b]
Fix for providing data to clerk task.
[*] [b] Binding [/b]
Additional re-binding options are now available. 
[*] [b] Translation [/b]
Translation fixes for German and French localization. Thank you every for reporting those to us! We highly appreciate that. Our community is amazing \o/

[list]
[*] Add game to exception folder in Windows Defender Firewall

notes.title: Devlog | Normandy
notes.content:
[h1]Builders![/h1]

[h3]We know that you loved our [b]area series[/b] and were patiently waiting for the next updates on that - so we're back!
[/h3]
As you might know - [b]it's Normandy week[/b] here, so introducing - [b][u]Normandy.[/u][/b]

According to history pages, landing in Normandy can be considered the biggest success during WW2, that had begun the victorious march to Berlin. This operation was able to be successful thanks to thorough and strict preparations, including counterintelligence operations that cause the enemy being unaware of the upcoming attack. 
That didn't change the fact that the Nazis have had quite fenced the coastline of Normandy - series of bunkers and trenches were placed through thousands of kilometers, supply depots were full of ammunition and coastal villages were used as stationers for the garrisons. A battery of anti-aircraft guns was put near the city of Longues-sur-Mer able to protect the area, including the beach and sea area in 2-kilometer radius. The information about next targets were sent from the observational bunker that was inserted in a small cliff closer to the sea. Except for that, in the fortification area was placed an ammunition bunker and small Tobruk-type bunker with machine guns and mortar sockets in them. For about and a day the complex was able to withhold the alliance far from its perimeter, but thanks to heavy bombing that had destroyed the infrastructure, the crew had surrendered.
After winning over the coastline, the alliance forces were pushing through the land to free the French villages and cities. It was often for them to see the magnitude of destruction caused by their own bombing on civilian structures while attacking Nazi bunkers. In the destroyed cities they could find the rest of the German forces - even after the surrender they could find some lone snipers harassing the alliance forces.

Okay, so what's interesting about our map that was created based on Normandy?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/9063e4e9ac106be98ee2ac874c047f6db7373c64.png[/img]
You've repaired that arched gate? Nice work!

It's always destroy, but when it's rebuilding time? Well how bout now on this church nave?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/34808d1e31f7e731d9fb1ca30eb0c1bfe010e7d5.png[/img]
Remember Harvest Moon? This is how it looks now - feel old yet? Now find those seeds and get to work!

Thanks for being with us during this journey, and we hope you're excited for upcoming stuff!

We are so happy that you enjoy our playtest. Thanks to you, we have so much feedback and interesting questions and ideas from you, that we've decided to do some Q&A this month.

[b]1) Will there be more options for buildings or potential sandbox aspect using a selection of pre-made walls, roofs and more decor?[/b]

Depends on the outcome of the interest - we could consider even a workshop. But for now - we're hoping for the best.

[b]2) Is there a possibility of changing the mechanics of building the walls? Actual one is quite tedious, especially with the highest level.[/b]

Only selective walls and defects are build with the use of bricks - rest of the buildings are build differently. In all full honesty, both mechanics have their fans, and we really want to keep the balance here.

[b]3) Will there be in the future the possibility of some kind of helpers in the game? Or even a multiplayer?[/b]

As before - we're keeping our fingers crossed that it will be a success. This will help in further development of the game.

[b]4) Will you plan to add a tool that will pick up more than one thing at a time while cleaning?[/b]

Hard question - we didn't think about it- we're happy to hear about your propositions.

[b]5) A cutscene after selecting the city of the main character travelling to the city would be an interesting idea. Is it a possibility that you would add something like this?[/b]

Each city will have their own cut-scene.

[b]6) We love what you show us now, and we also know the main locations of the game. But are there somehow plans to add more cities in the countries you have in the game?[/b]

Again - as in the first question. We're planning to add 2 more maps after the release, and maybe something else? We will see.

[b]7) The ability to unlock better equipment in an interesting option. Are you considering it?[/b]

Not really - our goal is to make each map as original as possible. Each has its own mechanics and tools. The only enhancements we are planning and working on are character-wise.

[b]8) Are you planning to add more countries, like Poland, maybe?[/b]

For now, we only can say that we're planning to add 2 DLC, but can't say more.

[b]9) The possibility of hearing the characters dub in their native language when we are playing in a particular country would be cool. Had you thought about it?[/b]

We thought about it, but don't think it's the best option for now.

[b]10) We could use vehicles like sledgehammer instead of a regular hammer or a sledge used for heavier destruction of objects. Are planning to add more equipment to the game?[/b]

The game has already implemented lots of different mechanics - we hope that you will enjoy what we had prepared in the full game.

That's all for now, folks! Next week we'll be back with another portion of most anticipated questions.

Till next time!

notes.title: Devlog #17 Hero of West Germany
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/55d7f2bf1d71d38291b5884c3174b9f33febba6d.png[/img]

[h1]Builders![/h1]

We’d already talked about the hero of the British campaign in WW2 Rebuilder, but for the last few weeks we’ve been showing you some of the maps taking place in Germany. New country means a new campaign with the brand new protagonist - let us introduce her now!

Ursula is the Trümmerfrau (ger. “rubble woman”). The German male population suffered great losses during World War II, with the soldiers being killed or taken captive. Women had to replace their fallen husbands, brothers, fathers and sons in many areas of everyday life. The ones that worked on clearing and rebuilding the ruined German cities were called Trümmerfrauen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/2807ce65514b6fa07447a891976186d9029483a5.png[/img]

Their life in after-war Germany was very hard. The cities were ruined beyond recognition, afterm firestorm-causing bombings. There was a shortage of food - Trümmerfrauen had been given for their work the food stamps barely covering their needs. Many of them lost their families during the war.

During her campaign Ursula, working on the rebuilds in various places in West Germany, looks for any traces of her missing husband Andreas, a German soldier that never came home. She begins her journey in Remagen, not far from the Golden Mile, the huge camp for the prisoners of war captured by the Allies. Here she renovates the famous Ludendorff bridge. She continues her search in Essen, helping with recovering the heavy machines from the city’s factories. The huge part of equipment of German industrial plants that survived the war had to be handed to the Allies as reparations. In Hamburg, the city devastated by firestorms, Ursula learns about her husband’s heroism in rescuing civilians. She also renovates the city’s canals and one of the tenement houses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/4938961dfcccf8b01a75395f020831ed005b1d1e.png[/img]

In WW2 Rebuilder we face a very sensitive task - showing the aftermath of World War II in Germany. We are trying our best to do it with utmost care and compassion for the victims of the most horrifying conflict in human history.

Is this the end of Ursula’s journey? Probably not, but we won’t talk about it now ;)
The WW2 Rebuilder Germany Prolog comes soon, stay tuned to experience the work of our Trümmerfrau yourself!

What do you think about Ursula and what do you expect from the German campaign? Let us know in the comments!

Till next time!

As you know already, playtests for our prologue and coming in big. And you all really like our stories about certain locations and maps. 

Let us continue our adventure and take this opportunity and introduce you further to the city of Hamburg.

In short after battle for Ruhr, the alliance took as it's next target the city of Hamburg. Operation Gomora was supposed to paralyze the biggest German docks and submarine factory complex. The goal was reached, although with difficulties in the future with setting the next goals caused by the smoke that was covering the building. All the docks and factories were destroyed according to the plan and pushed out of commission for at least a month.
Unfortunately, more than 3/4 of the city was destroyed with 40 thousand lives were taken by the ravages of war and explosions

What's our story?

Let us hear what our Hero has to say:
"I remember the paralyzing fear I felt reading in the newspapers about the bombings of Hamburg in 1943. My Andreas' unit was stationed in the city at the time. I was worried sick for weeks, and finally a letter from the Wehrmacht arrived: Andreas was severely burned but alive!
They say all the Allies wanted at the time was to stop the Nazi U-boat production. They succeeded, but at the same time Hamburg with its inhabitants burned almost completely. When the incendiary bombs penetrated through to the cellars full of coal, all hell broke loose
Now I arrive in Hamburg, witnessing the aftermath of the monstrous firestorms my husband had once encountered."

notes.title: Devlog #14 Ludendorff Bridge
notes.content:
[h1]Builders![/h1]

Don't you think we've stopped with our map series! We've just took a little break to recharge and now we're back to our journey.

As you all know Rebuilder consists of 3 cauntries at the cor- England, Germany and France. So yes, it's now time for some Germany areas- West Germany to be more percise.

Introducing- Ludendorff Bridge

During the mass invasion on Germany it was thought that the biggest difficulty would be getting to Berlin through the river Ren, because the alliance thought that germans had destroyed all of the bridges that could lead to the city. But when in 1945 american troops had arrived near the west side of Ren earlier than they had planned, it occured to them that the Ludendorf bridge near the city of Remagen was still intact, possibly being the last connection to Berlin.

The fight for the bridge, or to be more specific- to destroy it lasted for 10 days. The Nazis tried everything in their power to destroy the bridge before american troops had crossed over to the other side of Ren. Right in the very beggining of taking over the bridge by alliance at least 3 tons of explosives were detonated and during the offensive- different types of weapons like V2 missiles or prototypes that hadn't been used in regular operations.

The victory was on alliance side, but the bridge didn't surviwe all of the attacks and had collapsed. Luckily most of the alliance force had passed through the bridge and during that time there had been built an pontoon bridge and an extra truss.

Okay what's interesting about the location?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/4cd5d84c68e76c5743646fb88aeb7e84cfc45898.png[/img]

[h1]Builders![/h1]

Your positive feedback about what we're sharing with you gave us a path for future posts. So by popular demand, continuing the series:

Introducing-  [b]RAF Lympne[/b]

According to history pages, before WW2, Royal Air Force station was base for Cinque Ports Flying Club. Although RAF Lympne was only a temporary base for technical issues, receiving transport and preparing for the missions and not a pit stop, it was at risk of bombarding during the war. There was even a possibility of Hans Bauer, who was Hitler's personal pilot, kidnapping the Führer and hand him over as a prisoner, but the mission hadn't eventuated.

During the Battle of Britain, the whole airport was bombarded and was beyond usage. All the Cinque Ports Flying Club planes that hadn't been evacuated, were destroyed beyond repair. For most of the time, the airport was only used as an emergency base.
After the War, RAF Lympne went into civilian use, mostly as a UK - France route.

What's our story?

Our English Rebuilder is sent to RAF Lympne, Kent, on the south. There, the objective is to prepare the whole airport to become an air ferry port between UK and France. The goal is for daily transport of the supplies.

The English Rebuilder is a young man eager to work hard for his fellow countrymen's future. His hometown in central England avoided the war turmoil, and the boy himself was too young to enlist, even though he really wanted to.

As he writes in his memoir, he and other workers set on a train journey to London to help rebuild the capital. On the way they encountered the destroyed Gimbert Station that needed to be fixed before continuing the ride. When they reached London, they were sent to work on the Necropolis Station, where the experience gained in Gimbert came in handy during the tasks you could’ve read about in our other devlog. Finally, when the heavy equipment arrived, the Hero could start the real demolition and construction works in the City of London district.

The English Rebuilder faced in London some painful memories which, however, are the source of his determination:

Thanks to the sacrifice of his, as well as of many other pilots, originating not only from the states of the Commonwealth, but also from Poland and Czechoslovakia, there is still anything left to be rebuilt here.”

There are no words for how horrible and cruel the war is, but our game wants to bring some peace and hope for the future,

This week we want to introduce you to our second helpful giant with his friends- crane and wrecking ball!

Acording to the books, the model we are presenting to you is called a crawler. A crawler crane has its boom mounted on an undercarriage fitted with a set of crawler tracks that provide both stability and mobility. Crawler cranes range in lifting capacity from about 40 to 4,000 long tons (44.8 to 4,480.0 short tons; 40.6 to 4,064.2 t).[
Wide tracks spread the weight out over a great area and are far better than wheels at traversing soft ground without sinking in. A crawler crane is also capable of traveling with a load. Its main disadvantage is its weight, making it difficult and expensive to transport. 

Our crawler is designed to lift heavy objects and place them where you want to. Also while in the wehicle, you can lift and lower the hook.

notes.title: Devlog #3 St. Nicholas' Church
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/ec95c44479265ac005a20543e0072ed8bf8d0cb3.png[/img]

[h1]BUILDERS![/h1]

This time we want to bring you closer to one of really popular monument- St. Nicholas' Church. 
Hamburg, as many German cities, was ravaged by World War II.  You can see sometimes structures that pre-date the war and, then, lots of newer construction post-war.  And there are structures that perhaps were not totally lost but repaired/re-constructed.  But there are rarely any that remain as they were right when the war came to an end.  Plain and simple record of how the city looked.  St. Nicholas Church in the heart of Hamburg is one of those places that silently stand as a testimonial to the destruction of war, almost completely as it stood at the end of the war (minor repairs to the belltower).
Our model is based on the moment before it was destroyed by the bombs. You see, what we can see here are actually remains of rebuilded in 1870 church that went almost down in the fire in 1840. Fun fact is that at the moment of rebuilding it, the tower was the highest known edifice.

Check out those marvelous landscapes of our model:

Our team is currently working on refining the details of London - a map that will appear in WW2 Rebuilder.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/f7184cf8bf282bfa66327587dc2cef73ea2c1472.jpg[/img]

During the Second World War, London was stormed by over a thousand planes in a series of raids called The Blitz. The enormity of the destruction in the city was unimaginably large. The battle that took place over this beautiful city was divided into four phases, each of which left its mark on the people and buildings in the city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40090453/a15f184f3101d03dec7b50068a8c7cb2fc802208.jpg[/img]

London was one of the most damaged cities during World War II. As a result of multiple bombings, part of the city and the port district virtually ceased to exist. 
The rebuilding of London in our game will take place in the neighbourhood of the Cathedral of St. Paul. The Cathedral survived the London fire to such an extent that its white bricks turned red hot. St. Paul survived the bombing of World War II and became a symbol of London's persistence.

In our game, one of your tasks is to rebuild London. Will you face such a great challenge and restore the city to its former glory?
